reason: E1 and E3 show that 800 °C annealing forms a protective oxide and improves tribocorrosion resistance for specific HEAs, but the hypothesis extends this to a different alloy (FeCoNiMnCu) and assumes a self-healing mechanism without direct evidence. E2 describes corrosion damage on the same alloy, contradicting the premise of a robust protective layer. The key premise that rapid oxide reformation governs the coupled response is not directly supported by the cited evidence.

This oxide layer provides excellent tribocorrosion resistance
Rapid self-healing of the oxide layer governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response
